title: Shortest Palindrome by Adding Letters in Front

concept.title: Find the longest palindrome at the start
body: You may add letters only at the **front** of the word. Suppose the longest prefix of the word that is already a palindrome has length `p`. The remaining letters `s[p..]` are not covered, so the best you can do is to copy them in reverse order to the front: the result is `reverse(s[p:]) + s`. A longer palindromic prefix means fewer letters to add.

To find `p` fast, compare **hashes**: the prefix `s[0..i)` is a palindrome exactly when it equals its own reversal. The reversal of that prefix is a block of the reversed word, namely `rs[n-i..n)`. So prefix `i` is a palindrome when `hash(s[0..i)) == hash(rs[n-i..n))`. Try `i` from `n` down to 1 and stop at the first success.
The one-letter prefix is always a palindrome, so the loop always stops. With hashing each test costs O(1); the whole search is O(n).

statement: You may add letters only at the beginning of a word. Print the shortest palindrome you can make this way.
inputFormat: A single word of lowercase letters.
outputFormat: Print the shortest palindrome that ends with the given word.

examples.note: The prefix aacecaa is a palindrome; add one `a` in front: aaacecaaa.
Only a is a palindromic prefix: add dcb in front.

hints: Find the longest prefix of the word that is a palindrome.
The letters after that prefix, reversed, go to the front.
A prefix is a palindrome when its hash equals the hash of the matching block of the reversed word.

explanation: The longest palindromic prefix is found by comparing the hash of each prefix with the hash of its reversal; the rest of the word, reversed, is put in front.

code.python:
M1, M2 = 1000000007, 998244353
B1, B2 = 911382323, 972663749


def build_hash(s):
    n = len(s)
    h1 = [0] * (n + 1)
    h2 = [0] * (n + 1)
    p1 = [1] * (n + 1)
    p2 = [1] * (n + 1)
    for i, ch in enumerate(s):
        v = ord(ch) - 96
        h1[i + 1] = (h1[i] * B1 + v) % M1
        h2[i + 1] = (h2[i] * B2 + v) % M2
        p1[i + 1] = p1[i] * B1 % M1
        p2[i + 1] = p2[i] * B2 % M2
    return h1, h2, p1, p2


def sub_key(hash_data, l, r):
    h1, h2, p1, p2 = hash_data
    a = (h1[r] - h1[l] * p1[r - l]) % M1
    b = (h2[r] - h2[l] * p2[r - l]) % M2
    return a * M2 + b

s = input().strip()

n = len(s)
rs = s[::-1]
da = build_hash(s)
db = build_hash(rs)
p = 1
for i in range(n, 0, -1):
    if sub_key(da, 0, i) == sub_key(db, n - i, n):
        p = i
        break
print(s[p:][::-1] + s)
